title: Hysteroscopy
what: The doctor looks inside your womb with a thin tube with a camera. It goes in through the cervix, with no cuts. A sample can be taken or a polyp removed at the same time.
why: For bleeding between periods, heavy periods, polyps, infertility, failed IVF attempts, and bleeding after menopause.
duration: the exam usually takes 10 to 30 minutes, longer with treatment; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: If you have discharge, itching, or pain now. It may be an infection

prepare.title: When
prepare.text: It is usually done in the first half of your cycle, a few days after your period ends. Your doctor will set the day.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually a swab and blood tests are needed. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: A short exam is sometimes done without anesthesia. A treatment procedure is done under anesthesia through a vein. Your doctor will tell you which you will have.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If you will have anesthesia, usually no food or drinks for 6 hours. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

bring: Someone to take you home, if you have anesthesia
steps: You empty your bladder and lie on the gynecology chair
If you have anesthesia, medicine goes into a vein and you fall asleep
The doctor puts in a speculum and cleans the cervix
A thin tube with a camera goes in through the cervix, and fluid is used to open up the womb
The doctor looks at the womb and, if needed, takes a sample or removes a polyp
feel: Without anesthesia: a pulling pain, like period cramps. Tell your doctor
With anesthesia: you usually feel and remember nothing
Afterwards: mild cramps low in the belly
after: Light bloody spotting for a few days is normal
Usually for up to 2 weeks: no sex, tampons, baths, swimming pools, or saunas. Your doctor will tell you how long
After anesthesia, do not drive for the rest of the day
Sample results usually take 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Heavy bleeding: soaking a pad within an hour
A fever above 38 degrees, or severe belly pain

faq.a: Without anesthesia it is unpleasant, like strong period pain, but usually bearable. If you are afraid, ask about anesthesia.

faq.q: Can I get pregnant after a hysteroscopy?
faq.a: Yes. A hysteroscopy is often done to help you get pregnant. Your doctor will tell you when to start trying.

reminders.text: Hysteroscopy tomorrow. Bring your test results and pads. If you will have anesthesia, no food or drinks from the time your clinic gave you.
